assets.prompt:
Edit target: the provided Chinese Bian River handscroll concept image. Production background plate for an interactive 2D historical game.
Change only these elements: REMOVE EVERY HUMAN FIGURE throughout the image, including tiny people on the bridge and distant street, and REMOVE ALL BOATS, passengers, masts, sails and floating cargo in the water. Replace these areas with a fully painted continuous scene: complete the bridge rails and timber decking, shop woodwork and empty tables behind people, cobbled lanes and stone riverbank; fill former boat areas with believable water ripples. The mooring landing and empty mooring posts should remain.
Preserve the exact panorama camera framing and placement of the timber bridge on the left, paper shop on the right, tea tables and cargo landing in between, willow trees, distant city and beautiful fine ink and translucent mineral-watercolor style. Keep all static architectural and small paper/tool/teaware/basket details at equal high quality. Keep the same muted ivory gray-green wood-ochre palette and old silk texture. NO added humans, no human silhouettes, no statues, no animals, no boats. No text, no labels, no symbols or lettering in shop signs. This is a quiet EMPTY ENVIRONMENT PLATE, with open ground for independently composited characters and open water for animated boat cutouts. No UI. Preserve the wide approximately 3:1 composition.

Use the attached handscroll ONLY as a style reference. Create a NEW PRODUCTION CHARACTER SPRITE ATLAS on a genuinely TRANSPARENT background, not a scene.
A perfectly regular grid of EXACTLY 6 COLUMNS and EXACTLY 3 ROWS: 18 separate full-body images. Prefer a high-resolution 4:3 landscape sheet. Every cell has equal dimensions. Keep every figure fully within its own cell, with generous transparent margins and no overlap. In each cell the feet stand on the same baseline at 90% cell height and the head begins around 12%; same body height across poses. Show NO grid lines, NO letters, NO labels, NO numbers, NO ground or scenery, NO extra objects outside the figure, NO cast shadows.
Style: refined fine warm charcoal ink outlines and translucent mineral watercolor, richly drawn tiny cloth folds, natural small faces, five-to-six head proportions, lightly weathered fabric, matching the reference's hand-painted historical scroll. These are Northern Song Chinese commoners, NOT Japanese, NOT Qing, no cartoon geometry, no chibi, no 3D, no white matte.
The SAME SIX IDENTITIES are repeated in ALL THREE ROWS, in this exact column order left to right:
1) 小柳: slim young male paper-shop assistant, age about 22, neat topknot, muted willow-green long work robe, cream collar, dark cloth belt and cloth shoes; kind curious face.
2) 周伯: sturdy weathered male boatman about 60, tan cloth headwrap, short salt-and-pepper beard, gray-blue coarse belted work robe with practical sleeves and dark trousers and cloth shoes.
3) 阿成: lean energetic male porter about 30, rust-ochre short work robe, wrapped calves, head cloth, strong but ordinary physique, dark cloth shoes.
4) 何娘: woman tea-stall keeper about 40, neatly coiled pinned hair, muted warm ochre-brown robe with a pale simple apron, calm alert expression, sensible shoes.
5) 陈生: quiet young male traveler about 28, muted slate-gray scholar's robe, simple soft cloth cap, small pale fabric sachet at belt, modest expression.
6) 沈砚: elderly male painter about 62, thin gray beard, simple gray-sage long robe, small soft cap, holding a rolled painting album or brush, composed expression.
ROW 1: relaxed natural STANDING pose in a consistent slightly elevated three-quarter view, body faces slightly right; both feet visible, arms relaxed, each identity and costume clearly readable.
ROW 2: ACTIVE HELP pose for the same people: col1 leans a little forward pressing both hands downward toward an unseen paper table; col2 holds a small coil of rope across his waist; col3 bends elbows to lift a single bamboo basket within the cell; col4 offers one small ceramic teacup; col5 extends an open palm as if asking about his lost sachet; col6 examines a small open album. No table, dock, floor or scenery.
ROW 3: THANK-YOU pose: the same six people give a subtle polite Chinese nod or slight bow, hands together or gently at the waist; keep their clothing, head scale, hair and facial identities unchanged; preserve the exact foot baseline.
Anatomy must be plausible with exactly one head, two arms, two legs per figure, no fused hands, no duplicated limbs, no missing feet. Genuine transparent alpha throughout all space between the 18 figures.

Use the provided Chinese river handscroll ONLY as the style and boat-design reference. Create a NEW boat sprite atlas on genuine transparent alpha, exactly TWO COLUMNS by TWO ROWS of separate boats, a regular grid with generous clear padding. All four boats are in a slightly elevated three-quarter side view, hull bow points to the RIGHT. Keep each complete hull, oars, rigging and canopy fully inside its cell, no overlap.
Top left: medium wooden cargo boat, woven bamboo rounded canopy, bamboo baskets of tea on deck, no sail.
Top right: small narrow wooden sampan, one bamboo roof, a long oar resting inside, no sail.
Bottom left: large wooden trading boat, woven bamboo cabin canopy, a single LOW FURLED mast and tidy ropes, varied small baskets.
Bottom right: small passenger boat with an open timber pavilion canopy and folded cloth, no sail.
Northern Song Chinese river craft, fine irregular warm ink outlines, detailed weathered planks, translucent gray-green, ochre and tea-brown watercolor matching the reference. Readable sensible hull geometry, finite rigging, no fantasy junk superstructure. No people, no human silhouettes, no ground, NO WATER, NO WAVES, no reflections or cast shadows. Do not print the checkerboard; all area outside boats truly transparent. No letters, labels, numbers, grid lines, text or watermarks. Prefer a wide landscape image.

A single foreground willow foliage cutout for a fine-ink Chinese historical handscroll game, matching the attached reference's delicate warm ink and muted mineral watercolor. Genuine transparent alpha background. A gracefully curved thin willow bough enters from the UPPER RIGHT edge and cascades diagonally down toward the lower left, carrying many long slender olive gray-green willow leaves in fine irregular clusters. A little bark and twig detail, open airy gaps between dangling fronds; a few soft ochre leaves. The bough and complete leaf tips stay inside the image edges except the deliberate branch entry at top right. This is a sparse FOREGROUND OCCLUSION LAYER, not a full tree: NO trunk, no ground, no landscape, no sky, no river, no pots, no people, no text, no frame, no shadows, no paper backing, no opaque rectangle. All gaps between leaves truly transparent. Refined and natural, not repeated geometric leaf icons. Medium-wide horizontal composition.

Use the attached Chinese handscroll as a STYLE reference only. Create a NEW transparent game prop sprite atlas: EXACTLY FOUR equal COLUMNS by TWO equal ROWS, eight isolated objects/groups, no grid lines or labels, generous transparent margins, no overlap. Slight elevated three-quarter viewpoint, finely detailed warm ink and restrained mineral watercolor on the objects only; matching the historical Northern Song river market reference. All space outside the objects truly transparent, no paper-colored backing, no checkerboard printed into the image.
Top row, left to right:
1. A small stack of creamy blank handmade paper with two top paper corners curled upward in a breeze, a tiny bamboo brush resting beside it. NO table, no hand.
2. The SAME stack of paper now lying FLAT, a small smooth gray oval paperweight securing the upper right corner, same camera and same scale. NO table, no hand.
3. A simple small charcoal tea brazier with a weathered ceramic kettle, a hint of pale steam rising, no table and no ground.
4. A woven bamboo basket of new tea leaves with a blank small paper cargo tag tied to its handle, no writing.
Bottom row, left to right:
1. A small warm-gray tabby CAT curled up sleeping, full tail visible, no floor or cushion.
2. The SAME tabby CAT stretching with its front paws extended, exactly four legs and one head and one tail, no floor.
3. A pair of ordinary Chinese adult customers SEATED on two low wooden stools around a small low timber tea table, one gray-green robed worker and one ochre-robed traveler. Whole bodies, table, two bowls and a small plate visible; natural conversation, subtle expressions, plausible hands. This whole group fits inside its one cell. No shop background.
4. A practical wooden single-wheel handcart with two long handles and a small tied bundle, no person.
No logos, letters, numerals, decorative icons, interface, borders or water. No modern teapot or modern chairs. The first two paper sprites must be visually the same paper stack apart from fluttering vs secured. The cat sprites must preserve the same identity.
